body.html: Arnoma Grand Bangkok has been a fixture of the Ratchaprasong intersection since it opened in 1988. The address — 99 Ratchadamri Road — places it squarely at the heart of Bangkok's most hotel-dense district: CentralWorld is directly across the street, Gaysorn Village is next door, the Erawan Shrine is a three-minute stroll, and Police General Hospital is 290 metres up the road. That last detail matters most for the bulk of guests who choose this hotel: patient families and outpatients who need to walk to the hospital every morning and evening without flagging a taxi through Bangkok rush-hour traffic.

The hotel runs 369 rooms across three categories: Superior (28 sqm), Deluxe (34 sqm) and Junior Suite (42 sqm). Multiple reviews praise the room sizes as more generous than expected at this price point, with Deluxe rooms adding a sofa and bathtub that longer-stay guests consistently mention as a worthwhile upgrade. Rooms are fitted with a minibar, kettle and complimentary Wi-Fi. The honest caveat — and it comes up across Booking.com, TripAdvisor and KAYAK reviews — is that the building's 1988 origins show in some rooms: décor can feel dated, the odd review mentions musty odour or a dripping tap, and power outlets near the bed are fewer than modern travellers expect.

"Best location I've ever stayed at — CentralWorld right across the street, walked to Police General Hospital in minutes, staff were genuinely friendly. Rooms are a bit old though; check recent photos before you book."

The facilities sit comfortably above the midrange bar. There is both an outdoor and an indoor pool, a gym, a sauna, and an Aroma Thai Spa. Dining options inside the hotel cover Mango 99 (a popular weekday lunch buffet), Arnoma Bakery, Arnoma Terrace and the Camelot Wine Pub, with 24-hour room service rounding things out. What guest reviews mention most consistently — aside from the location — is staff quality: front-desk teams, porters and housekeeping are frequently singled out for warmth and responsiveness, which matters considerably when you're staying under stressful medical circumstances. Free parking is also available, a genuine rarity on Ratchadamri Road.

The location score of 9.4 out of 10 on Trip.com is not a surprise to anyone who knows this intersection. Very few 4-star hotels in Bangkok can match this address for walkability: CentralWorld straight ahead, Big C Ratchadamri a short walk, the Erawan Shrine in three minutes, BTS Ratchadamri in five minutes, BTS Chit Lom in eight. A skywalk system links the hotel area to CentralWorld and the BTS, keeping the walk comfortable even during Bangkok's afternoon downpours. For patients attending Police General Hospital, the hospital itself is a four-minute walk north along the pavement — no overpasses, no road crossings needed.

Being straightforward about the downsides: the renovation cycle has not been uniform across all 369 rooms. Reviews from Booking.com and TripAdvisor note that some room categories still carry an older look and feel, and a small number report minor maintenance issues such as musty smells or inadequate hot water. Wi-Fi, while included, gets mixed reports on upper floors — most guests had no issues, but it's worth testing on arrival and speaking to the front desk if the signal is weak. Pricing follows a wide seasonal swing: low-season rates (May–July) start around ฿2,200 per night, while the peak December–January window can push well past ฿3,500, so checking rates across platforms before booking is worthwhile.

Arnoma Grand Bangkok competes on its own terms. This is not the most polished 4-star in Bangkok, but it offers a prime-location address at a midrange price — and for anyone whose primary reason for being in the Ratchaprasong area is Police General Hospital, no other hotel at this price tier comes closer. Guests who leave happy consistently cite the same two things: staff attitude and location. Those who leave disappointed usually expected a recently renovated room and got something older instead. Setting expectations correctly before booking is the whole game here.

honestSummary: Arnoma Grand Bangkok sells its location far more than its room design — 290 m from Police General Hospital, walkable to every major landmark at Ratchaprasong, with good staff and free parking. The honest trade-off is a building that opened in 1988 and has not been uniformly renovated: some rooms feel fresh, others feel dated. If the hospital is your reason for being here, few hotels in Bangkok offer this combination of proximity, mid-range price and genuine walkability.
honestChecks: If you expect a fully renovated, contemporary room — some categories have been updated while others retain a noticeably older feel. Check recent room photos on the booking platform and consider upgrading to Deluxe or Junior Suite, which tend to be better maintained.

If you're staying over the Christmas or New Year period — high-season rates (Dec–Jan) can exceed ฿3,500 per night, a significant jump from the low-season base. Compare rates across Agoda, Booking and Trip.com and book well in advance for the best price.

If reliable Wi-Fi for remote work is essential — a minority of reviews report inconsistent signal on upper floors. Test the connection immediately after check-in and ask the front desk to assist; most connectivity issues reported are resolved quickly by staff.

tips.title: Walking to Police General Hospital
tips.body: Exit the hotel and follow the Ratchadamri Road pavement north. The hospital entrance is roughly 290 m away — about four minutes at a normal pace, with a level pavement and no road crossings required.

tips.title: Two BTS stations within reach
tips.body: BTS Ratchadamri is about 5 minutes south on foot; BTS Chit Lom is about 8 minutes north. Pick the one that suits your direction. The CentralWorld skywalk keeps the walk dry during Bangkok's afternoon rains.

tips.title: Mango 99 weekday lunch buffet
tips.body: The Mango 99 restaurant runs a reasonably priced weekday lunch buffet — useful on days when you don't want to venture out. Hotel members get a 10% F&B discount across all dining venues.

tips.title: Free parking — make the most of it
tips.body: The hotel offers complimentary in-building parking for guests. In a district where street and mall parking is both scarce and expensive, this is a genuinely useful perk if you have a car.

faqTitle: Frequently Asked Questions — Arnoma Grand Bangkok

faq.q: Where is Arnoma Grand Bangkok and how far is it from Police General Hospital?
faq.a: The hotel is at 99 Ratchadamri Road, Lumphini, Pathum Wan, Bangkok 10330, directly opposite CentralWorld and next to Gaysorn Village. Police General Hospital is approximately 290 metres north along the Ratchadamri pavement — a flat, four-minute walk with no road crossings.

faq.q: Which BTS station do I use for Arnoma Grand Bangkok?
faq.a: BTS Ratchadamri is the closest, about a 5-minute walk south of the hotel and convenient for the Silom Line. BTS Chit Lom is about 8 minutes north and better for the Sukhumvit Line. A skywalk system connecting CentralWorld and the BTS keeps the walk sheltered from sun and rain. Don Mueang Airport is roughly 21 km away (about 30 minutes by car).

faq.q: What does a room at Arnoma Grand Bangkok cost and which type should I book?
faq.a: Rates start from around ฿2,200 per night for a Superior Room (28 sqm). Deluxe Rooms (34 sqm, from ~฿2,800) add a sofa and bathtub and are recommended for stays of two or more nights. Junior Suites (42 sqm, from ~฿3,800) offer the most space. High-season pricing (Dec–Jan) can significantly exceed these figures — compare rates across platforms and book ahead.

faq.q: Is Arnoma Grand Bangkok a good choice for patient families staying near Police General Hospital?
faq.a: Yes, for several practical reasons. The 290 m walk to the hospital entrance takes about four minutes on a level pavement — no taxis, no traffic. The hotel has on-site restaurants, Big C Ratchadamri is nearby for groceries, and CentralWorld is directly opposite for anything else. Free in-building parking is available if you have a car, and staff are consistently rated as warm and helpful — an important factor when staying under difficult circumstances.

faq.q: Are the rooms at Arnoma Grand Bangkok dated? What should I check before booking?
faq.a: The hotel opened in 1988 and renovation has not been applied uniformly to all room categories. Some rooms have a noticeably older look and feel. The practical advice: look at the most recent room photos on the platform you're booking through, consider choosing Deluxe or Junior Suite (which tend to be better maintained), and read reviews from the past three to six months for the most accurate picture.

faq.q: What facilities does Arnoma Grand Bangkok have?
faq.a: The hotel has both an outdoor and an indoor swimming pool, a gym, a sauna and an Aroma Thai Spa. Dining options include Mango 99 (weekday lunch buffet), Arnoma Bakery, Arnoma Terrace and the Camelot Wine Pub, with 24-hour room service. Free Wi-Fi is provided in all rooms. Free in-building parking is available for guests. The hotel does not accept pets. Check-in is at 2:00 PM and check-out at 12:00 PM.
